Streaming market data over IBKR's WebSocket, and the transport underneath it open to every other topic IBKR publishes. **90 of IBKR's 108 Trading endpoints, plus the socket.**

```sh
dotnet add package IbkrDotNet.Extensions.DependencyInjection --prerelease
```

## What is new

`IMarketDataStreamClient` is the streaming counterpart of `IMarketDataClient`: the same tick numbers and the same values, pushed as IBKR updates them rather than fetched on request.

```csharp
await foreach (var quote in ibkr.MarketDataStream.SubscribeAsync(conId, MarketDataField.TopOfBook, cancellationToken: ct))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{quote.LastPrice} {quote.BidPrice}/{quote.AskPrice} at {quote.UpdatedAt}");
}
```

Nothing is sent until the loop starts. The first read opens the socket — which needs the brokerage session, like everything else behind `/iserver` — and sends `smd`. Leaving the loop, by `break`, cancellation or an exception, sends `umd`, so the instrument's market data line is released. IBKR ends a stream fifteen minutes after it was requested; the client re-sends the request every ten (`Streaming.MarketDataRenewalInterval`) for as long as the loop runs, so a long read sees no gap.

Underneath is `IIbkrStreamingTransport`: one socket per session, opened with the brokerage session's cookie and the mechanism's credential on the upgrade request, `tic` every thirty seconds, reconnection with exponential backoff that re-sends every open subscription, and one read loop demultiplexed into per-topic subscriptions. It is public for the same reason `IIbkrApiClient` is. Any topic IBKR publishes — orders, trades, profit and loss, the account ledger and summary, the price ladder, historical bars — is reachable through `SubscribeAsync` with authentication, keep-alive and reconnection intact, the body arriving as a `JsonElement` or deserialized into a record of your own. `StreamingTopics` names every topic; `system`, `sts`, `blt` and `ntf` have models.

A slow reader never stalls the socket. A subscription holds one message by default and drops the oldest, so a reader that falls behind is handed the latest quote next rather than a backlog, and `DroppedMessages` says how many it missed. There is deliberately no wait mode: every subscription shares the one read loop, and a consumer that could block it would stall every other subscription on the socket.

`AddIbkrTrading` registers the transport as a singleton and the stream client over it, binds a `Streaming` section from configuration and validates it at startup, so a bad interval fails when the host starts rather than when the socket first opens. Both hang off `IIbkrTradingClient` as `Streaming` and `MarketDataStream`. Disposing the container closes the socket.

## Two keep-alives, not one

`tic` keeps the socket alive. It does not keep the brokerage session behind it alive: the REST `/tickle` still has to run, so `AddBrokerageSessionKeepAlive()` is as necessary with a stream open as without. The `api=` cookie that `/tickle` returns is also what the upgrade request presents, which is why opening the socket goes through `EnsureBrokerageSessionAsync` first.

## Breaking changes

`IIbkrTradingClient` has two new members, `Streaming` and `MarketDataStream`, and the `IbkrTradingClient` constructor takes the two services behind them. An implementation of the interface outside this repository — a test double, typically — needs both members; an instance built by hand rather than resolved from the container needs the two arguments. That is the whole of it: the public API transcript gained 249 lines and lost one, the old constructor.

`IIbkrAuthenticator` also gained `GetStreamingCredentialAsync`, as a default interface method returning `null`, so an authenticator written outside this repository keeps compiling and gets the gateway's behaviour — nothing beyond the session cookie on the upgrade request. OAuth 2.0 presents its session token as `bearer_token` and OAuth 1.0a its access token as `oauth_token`, as IBKR documents.

## Why this is a prerelease

The socket has been driven end to end over a scripted `WebSocket` — reassembly of a message across frames, drop and reopen, server close, renewal on the interval, `umd` on `break` and on cancellation, the failure surfacing when reconnection is off — and not yet against a live gateway. The upgrade request against a real gateway is the one part no fake reproduces, and the `.live.json` fixture that would pin IBKR's real `smd` message is still to be captured. Every entry in the [reference](https://github.com/jerbersoft/ibkrdotnet#things-about-ibkr-that-will-otherwise-surprise-you) came from a live gateway doing something the documentation does not say, and the socket has not had that pass.

The streaming group in `samples/IbkrDotNet.Samples.Verify` exists for exactly that: it opens the socket, reads the `system` confirmation and the `sts` status IBKR sends on connect, sends `tic`, streams one contract to its first message and prints that message in full. It is the first thing to run.

551 tests, 89 of them new since `v0.3.0-preview.1`. The fixtures are IBKR's documented examples for `system`, `sts`, `blt` and `ntf`, and the IBM top-of-book message from its streaming guide.

## About the version

`v0.3.0-preview.1` said `0.3.0` proper would follow once the publishing path had proven itself. The path did — that version is on nuget.org with its commit recorded — but `0.3.0` was defined as the `v0.2.0` surface with no API changes, and this tree is not that. Streaming is a minor version by any reading, so the number moves to `0.4.0`, and the suffix stays because every version before `1.0.0` is a prerelease while the public API settles.

## Not in this release

Market data is the one topic with a typed client; the rest are read through the transport, and `act` account updates arrive as raw JSON. The remaining 18 endpoints are the two Financial Advisor groups, tracked as [#21](https://github.com/jerbersoft/ibkrdotnet/issues/21) and [#22](https://github.com/jerbersoft/ibkrdotnet/issues/22); `IIbkrApiClient` reaches them today.

## Publishing

Pushed by [Trusted Publishing](https://learn.microsoft.com/nuget/nuget-org/trusted-publishing) over OIDC, as `v0.3.0-preview.1` was; both packages are also attached to this release.
